description: Somos un equipo enfocado en el desafío de crear un juego espacial. Buscamos integrantes para colaborar en la programación, diseño o aportando ideas para el proyecto. No requerimos conocimientos avanzados, solo disposición para aprender y trabajar juntos durante la hackatón. Cualquiera que desee participar es bienvenido.
summary:
NOCTURNE is an educational game that helps school-age learners discover the stories behind NASA hardware on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space. Guided by a curious mouse companion, players enter a library of interactive space adventures in English or Spanish.

Its main story, Mars Jelly: Sweet Horizon, follows an Opportunity-inspired rover through exploration, discovery, and a dust storm, introducing the relationship between sunlight, solar power, and a mission’s lasting scientific legacy. Separate adventures explore lunar laser ranging, Voyager 1, Mars exploration, and space heritage.

Built with Godot and browser-based minigames, NOCTURNE combines playful interaction, stylized art, and NASA-informed storytelling. It addresses the challenge by connecting spacecraft and instruments to the discoveries they made possible. Our aim is to turn curiosity into questions: What did this equipment do? What did it teach us? Why does its story still matter?
details:
NOCTURNE turns space-mission history into an interactive learning experience. Designed for school-age space enthusiasts, it connects NASA hardware with the questions, discoveries, and human effort behind it.

The experience begins with Nocturne, a stylized mouse companion that players can care for and interact with. A Stories library connects this playful introduction to educational adventures. The main application runs in Godot, while four additional HTML adventures open separately in a browser.

The main story, Mars Jelly: Sweet Horizon, lets players drive an Opportunity-inspired rover through a stylized Martian landscape. Waypoint objectives guide a four-act narrative about exploration, solar energy, a dust storm, and scientific legacy. Its terrain, dialogue, and character emotions are fictionalized; they are not NASA terrain measurements or actual rover transmissions. Players can return to the mouse-care scene without resetting its progress.

The library also includes:

  • Oppy: An Adventure on Mars: introduces rover exploration, observations, photography, and solar energy.
  • Voyager 1: introduces spacecraft journeys and the scientific purpose of deep-space exploration.
  • The Silent Mirror: explains how reflected light and round-trip travel time can help measure the Earth–Moon distance.
  • Keepers of the Legacy: encourages learners to recognize and document space hardware and consider its historical value.
  • An illustrated native reader: provides additional mission stories and NASA imagery when an internet connection is available.

The browser adventures include learning questions, hints, and a three-medal learning passport. English is the default language, with optional Spanish support. Care progress and preferences are saved, while browser adventures store their progress separately. Mars Jelly currently restarts when reopened.

Our intended impact is to encourage curiosity about science and help learners connect a piece of equipment with the knowledge it made possible. The project supports exploration and discussion; classroom learning outcomes have not yet been measured.

NOCTURNE combines a virtual companion, comic-inspired visuals, jelly-like materials, interactive missions, and an emotional narrative. The mouse is a fictional guide, while mission information is attributed to NASA/JPL resources. Space heritage is presented as something to understand, document, and protect.

Development tools include Godot 4.3, GDScript, Godot shaders, Blender, Python, HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Canvas/SVG, Web Audio, JSON, Git, and GitHub. ChatGPT and OpenAI Codex assisted with programming, debugging, translations, documentation, and visual design. OpenAI image generation produced the laboratory background. Development and testing took place on Windows computers.

The public repository includes source code, assets, setup instructions, references, license notices, and AI-use disclosures. It retains MIT licensing for new original contributions and Apache-2.0 for the imported Nocturne/Mars Jelly code, alongside existing third-party notices.

Testing in Godot 4.3 covered mission launch, rover movement, waypoint progression, returning to the library, language selection, and resizing. Automated complete-story checks accelerated dialogue and moved the rover to objectives. Mars Jelly currently requires a keyboard and mouse; no tested Android release or live telemetry processing is claimed.
